questions.question:
Who of the following was receiver of Bharat Ratna award?

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Both I and II**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Lata Mangeshkar** was awarded the Bharat Ratna, India's highest civilian honor, in 2001.
 
• **Bhupen Hazarika** received the Bharat Ratna posthumously in 2019.
 
• The Bharat Ratna is conferred in recognition of exceptional service/performance of the highest order in any field of human endeavor.
 
• It is the highest civilian award in India, instituted on 2 January 1954.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Bharat Ratna**

 
 
• The Bharat Ratna is the highest civilian award in India, given for exceptional service in any field.
 
• It was instituted on 2 January 1954 by the President of India.
 
• The award consists of a Sanad (certificate) signed by the President and a medallion.
 
• There is no formal provision that the award should be given to Indian citizens only. It has been awarded to a naturalized citizen (Mother Teresa) and to two non-Indians (Khan Abdul Ghaffar Khan and Nelson Mandela).
 
 
 
• **Lata Mangeshkar**
 
 
• Renowned playback singer, known as the "Nightingale of India".
 
• She has sung songs in over thirty-six regional Indian languages and foreign languages.
 
• She was awarded the Bharat Ratna in 2001, recognizing her contributions to the Indian music industry.
 
 
 
• **Bhupen Hazarika**
 
 
• An Indian playback singer, lyricist, musician, poet, and film-maker from Assam.
 
• He is known for his works in Assamese, Bengali, and Hindi cinema.
 
• He was posthumously awarded the Bharat Ratna in 2019.

questions.question: Who among the following was the youngest recipient of the Padma Vibhushan award in dance in 1986?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Birju Maharaj**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Pandit Birju Maharaj **was the youngest recipient of the **Padma Vibhushan Award** in **dance in 1986**.
 
• Maharaj achieved the distinction of being one of the youngest artists to receive the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award, being honored at the age of 28.
 
• Pandit Birju Maharaj, an eminent figure in Indian arts, was not only a dancer but also a composer, singer, and exponent of the **Lucknow "Kalka-Bindadin" **Gharana of Kathak dance.
 
• Hailing from the illustrious Maharaj family of Kathak dancers, he was preceded by notable figures such as his uncles, Shambhu Maharaj and Lachhu Maharaj, as well as his father and guru, Acchan Maharaj.
 
• Maharaj also delved into Hindustani classical music, showcasing his prowess as a vocalist. Having collaborated with his uncle, Shambhu Maharaj, at Bhartiya Kala Kendra, later known as Kathak Kendra, New Delhi, Maharaj assumed leadership at the latter institution for several years.
 
• Following his retirement in 1998, he established his own dance school, Kalashram, located in Delhi.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

__

• **Abhimanyu Lal,** on the other hand, is a distinguished Indian classical Kathak dancer, choreographer, and percussionist. He inherits his artistry from his renowned Kathak mentor, Guru Geetanjali Lal, as her son and disciple. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The Padma Vibhushan,** **India's second-highest civilian award **following the **Bharat Ratna,** was established on** 2 January 1954, **to honor individuals for their exceptional and distinguished service.
 
• Open to all individuals irrespective of race, occupation, position, or gender, the award excludes government servants, except doctors and scientists, along with those employed in PSUs.
 
• Since its inception, the award has been conferred upon 336 individuals, including thirty-one posthumous recipients and twenty-one non-citizen honorees.
 
• Notable among the inaugural recipients in 1954 were luminaries such as Satyendra Nath Bose, Nand Lal Bose, Zakir Husain, Balasaheb Gangadhar Kher, Jigme Dorji Wangchuck, and V. K. Krishna Menon.

• Kathak dance

 
 
• ​One of the eight primary styles of Indian classical dance is kathak.
 
• It is an Uttar Pradesh classical dancing style. The storytellers or itinerant bards known as Kathakars in ancient northern India are often credited as the creators of Kathak.
 
• The Vedic Sanskrit words Katha, which means "story," and Kathakar, which means "the one who tells a story" or "to do with stories," are the roots of the word Kathak.
 
• Traveling Kathakars used dance, songs, and music to transmit tales from the great epics and ancient mythology. Kathak dancers use intricate footwork, flexible body movements, and, most importantly, expressive face expressions to convey a variety of stories.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• ** Kathakali**

 
 
• Kathakali is a classical dance form that originates from Kerala, a state in the southern part of India.
 
• It is distinguished by its vibrant costumes, elaborate makeup, and face masks that the performers wear.
 
• Kathakali translates to "Story-Play" and is known for its intricate storytelling, detailed gestures, and expressive eye movements.
 
• The dance form combines dance, music, drama, and literature into a composite art form, making it unique and complex.
 
• Themes of Kathakali are mostly taken from the Indian epics like Mahabharata, Ramayana, and other ancient scriptures.
 
• It is performed exclusively by men and involves rigorous physical training to master the art form.
 
• The music used in Kathakali is called Sopanam and is sung in the Malayalam language.
 
 
 
• **Kuchipudi **
 
 
• One of the eight principal Indian classical dances is Kuchipudi.
 
• It comes from the Andhra Pradesh state of India, specifically the village of Kuchipudi.
 
• Kuchipudi was created as a way to worship Krishna, a Hindu deity.
 
• Siddhendra Yogi, a gifted poet and visionary who belonged to the Vaishnava sect and had the ability to give some of his visions solid form, created the Kuchipudi style of Yakshagaana in the 17th century.
 
• Kuchipudi is renowned for its dynamic storytelling, dramatic characterization, outstanding, rapid dancing, and expressive eye movements.
 
• Tandava (the regal, masculine) and Lasya (lyrical graceful and feminine energy) are combined in this dance.

• **​Bharatnatyam**

• Bharatnatyam is also known as *Dashiattam*.
 
• Elements of Bharatnatyam:
 
 
• Alarippu-seeking blessing of god with simple dance steps in rhythm.
 
• Jatiswaram-Nritta component with devoid expression.
 
• Shabdam-dramatic element with expressed words.
 
• Varnam-combination of dance and emotion to express a story.
